content: Is there a simple way to obtain a topologically sorted list of all Mathlib modules? (I.e., such that a module is only listed after all its depenencies have been listed.)

• There have been ≥ 2 PRs that tried to add a script for it but ended up closing (out of lost interest I think)
  • The easiest solution IMO is to download the current import-graph from CI and load it into Python's networkx
  • You can also use functions from ImportGraph if you prefer

1. Go to the CI run on the current master commit
  2. Download the import-graph artifact below and unzip to get import_graph.dot
  3. pip install networkx pydot
  4. import networkx as nx
  5. g = nx.drawing.nx_pydot.read_dot('.../import_graph.dot')
  6. list(nx.topological_sort(g))

IMO loading the graph into networkx is useful even beyond topological sorting, e.g. I use it to find common ancestors to know where to place theorems.
Can I just run lake build with some options, so that it outputs what it would build, but without actually building anything?

I don't think so (it doesn't seem to have --dry-run) but idk.
You can lake exe graph ./import-graph.pdf if it helps.
